Running the backend on a cluster¶

On a SLURM cluster the backend runs in an Apptainer container on a compute node, not on the frontend (the login node), and the desktop reaches it through an SSH tunnel. Two scripts do this:

  • scripts/launch_backend_slurm.sh, run on the frontend, submits the job, waits for the backend to answer and prints the tunnel command and the token;

  • scripts/visivo_slurm_tunnel.sh, run on the laptop, does the same over SSH, opens the tunnel itself and keeps it open.

Both print their full help with --help. A multi-node variant that spreads the heavy computations over a Dask cluster is described below.

Quick start¶

From the laptop, with key-based SSH access to the frontend and a clone of the repository in the frontend’s home:

bash scripts/visivo_slurm_tunnel.sh \
    --frontend <frontend> --user <user> \
    --partition gpu --gres gpu:1 \
    --data-root /path/to/data \
    --sif ~/VisIVOVisualAnalytics/backend-egl.sif \
    --port 18900

When it reports the tunnel ready, register the backend in the desktop under Settings ▸ Backends ▸ Remote Backends with the URL it prints (http://localhost:18900), the token (also saved in ~/.visivo_slurm_token on the laptop) and, for an SRC node, the node’s code in the SKAVA catalogue. bash scripts/visivo_slurm_tunnel.sh --stop closes the tunnel and cancels the job.

Tip

The helper’s local port defaults to 18900, not to the port of the desktop’s local backend (8000 by default). Keep it that way if you pass --port: the desktop treats a loopback URL on its local backend’s port as the local backend and, when a local token exists (VISIVO_TOKEN or ~/.visivo_token), sends that instead of the one registered for the entry, which the cluster backend then refuses.

The launcher: launch_backend_slurm.sh¶

The launcher writes a batch script, submits it with sbatch, waits for the compute node to be assigned (up to VISIVO_ASSIGN_TIMEOUT seconds, 300 by default, set in the frontend’s environment), then polls the backend’s /v1/health over SSH from the frontend to the compute node until it answers. It then prints the job id, the compute node, the port, the ssh -N -L command to run on the laptop, and the entries for the desktop’s Backends page.

The token is saved, readable only by you, to ~/.visivo_token on the frontend, or to <workspace>/token with a workspace. A job that was given a GPU declares it in the status document (VISIVO_NODE_GPU=1, otherwise 0).

The workspace¶

With --workspace DIR the launcher creates and binds (at the same path):

Path

Used as

DIR/exports

the backend’s workspace exports (VISIVO_EXPORTS_DIR): products such as cutouts, moment maps and finder outputs. It is also a data root (VISIVO_DATA_ROOTS is the data root, if any, plus this directory), so a product opens where it was written.

DIR/cache/hips, DIR/cache/numba, DIR/cache/cupy

the HiPS, Numba and CuPy caches

DIR/logs

the job logs (unless VISIVO_LOG_DIR is set)

DIR/token

the token file

Other backend settings¶

The launcher passes only the settings above into the container. Any other backend variable, for example VISIVO_RENDER_MAX_SESSIONS or VISIVO_FULL_RES_THRESHOLD_BYTES, can be exported with the APPTAINERENV_ prefix in the shell the launcher runs in: sbatch hands that environment to the job, and Apptainer passes APPTAINERENV_<NAME> into the container as <NAME>.

export APPTAINERENV_VISIVO_RENDER_MAX_SESSIONS=4
bash scripts/launch_backend_slurm.sh --sif backend-egl.sif ...

The laptop helper: visivo_slurm_tunnel.sh¶

The helper runs the launcher on the frontend over SSH, reads the job id, the compute node, the port and the token from its output, and opens the tunnel localhost:<port> to <node>:<port> through the frontend.

Option

Default

Meaning

--frontend HOST

required

The SLURM frontend.

--user USER

$USER

The SSH login on the frontend.

--repo-dir DIR

VISIVO_REMOTE_REPO, else VisIVOVisualAnalytics

The clone on the frontend, relative to the remote home.

--port N

VISIVO_PORT, else 18900

The local port of the tunnel. When given, it is also passed to the launcher, so the backend listens on the same port on the node; otherwise the backend listens on the launcher’s default and the tunnel maps one to the other.

--stop

Stop the tunnel, cancel the job and remove the token file.

any other option

Passed unchanged to the launcher (--partition, --gres, --sif, --data-root, --node-code, --workspace, …).

The helper:

  • checks before submitting anything: it refuses to start while a tunnel from an earlier run is still active (stop it first with --stop) or while the local port is already in use, so a job is never submitted that its tunnel could not reach;

  • keeps the tunnel open: ssh runs in a loop in the background, with keep-alives (ServerAliveInterval=15, ServerAliveCountMax=4) so a dead connection is noticed within about a minute, and is started again three seconds after it ends (a network change, the laptop sleeping). It runs non-interactively (BatchMode), so it needs key-based SSH access to the frontend;

  • reports ready only when the backend answers through the tunnel: it polls /v1/health on the local port for up to 30 s. If the backend does not answer, it closes the tunnel and says that the job is still queued or running (--stop cancels it);

  • saves the token in ~/.visivo_slurm_token on the laptop, readable only by you. It is never written to ~/.visivo_token: that file belongs to the desktop’s local backend, and the desktop would then fail to authenticate against it.

--stop ends the reconnect loop (and the ssh it started), runs scancel on the frontend for the job it recorded (~/.visivo_slurm_job) and removes ~/.visivo_slurm_token.

Multi-node backend with Dask¶

scripts/launch_backend_slurm_dask.sh allocates several nodes, starts a Dask scheduler and Dask workers on the first node, Dask workers on each of the others, and the backend on the first node with VISIVO_DASK_SCHEDULER pointing at the scheduler, so heavy operations (moment maps, channel maps) are spread over all the workers. scripts/visivo_slurm_tunnel_dask.sh is its laptop helper.

Launcher options (on the frontend):

Option

Environment default

Default

Meaning

--nodes N

VISIVO_NODES

4

Nodes to allocate.

--cpus N

VISIVO_CPUS

32

CPUs per node.

--workers N

VISIVO_WORKERS_PER_NODE

the value of --cpus

Dask workers per node (one thread each).

--gres G

VISIVO_GRES

empty (no GPU)

GPUs per node.

--partition, --mem, --time, --port, --bind, --data-root, --sif, --backend-src, --token, --no-gpu

as for the single-node launcher

It has no --workspace, --node-code or --version. The scheduler listens on port 18786 and its dashboard on 18787 of the first node; the backend itself runs with four local workers. The token is written to ~/.visivo_token on the frontend, and the scheduler and worker logs go to ~/.visivo_logs.

Helper options (on the laptop): --frontend, --user, --repo-dir and --port as above, plus --dashboard-port P (the local port of a second tunnel to the Dask dashboard, default VISIVO_DASHBOARD_PORT or 18787) and --no-dashboard (no dashboard tunnel). Every other option goes to the Dask launcher. The token is saved in ~/.visivo_slurm_dask_token; --stop closes both tunnels and cancels the job.

The Dask helper behaves like the single-node one: it refuses to start while an earlier tunnel or job is recorded or a local port is taken (and when --port and --dashboard-port are the same), reopens either tunnel when it drops, records the job as soon as the launcher prints its id, and is ready only when the backend answers through the tunnel.

Apptainer images¶

The definitions are in apptainer/. Build them from the repository root (the paths in their %files and %setup sections are relative to it).

Definition

Base

What it contains

backend.def

python:3.12-slim

The slim image. No VTK, Numba or llvmlite (no usable install on POWER9 from PyPI): no isosurfaces, no velocity-field products, no server-side rendering, and the moment kernels run unaccelerated. ENABLE_CUPY=1 and ENABLE_SOFIA=1 at build time add CuPy and SoFiA-2 (export them as APPTAINERENV_ENABLE_CUPY and APPTAINERENV_ENABLE_SOFIA: Apptainer passes only prefixed variables into the build).

backend-conda.def

condaforge/miniforge3

The full scientific stack from conda-forge (Numba, VTK, healpy), for ppc64le, x86_64 and aarch64, with SoFiA-2 (from conda-forge, or built from source where there is no package; the build does not fail without it). CuPy with APPTAINERENV_ENABLE_CUPY=1 at build time. The recommended base for an SRC node.

backend-x86.def

condaforge/mambaforge

x86_64 with NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs (CUDA 12.8 runtime, CuPy on by default; NVIDIA driver 570 or later on the host).

backend-conda-egl.def

backend-conda.sif (local image)

The conda image with VTK rebuilt from source with EGL, for server-side 3-D rendering on the node’s GPU. Built as backend-egl.sif.

backend-egl-h265-overlay.def

backend-egl.sif (local image)

Not up to date, as its own help says: it targets an earlier EGL image that kept the stack in conda’s base environment, so it would install FFmpeg, PyAV and aiortc where the backend does not look. Server-side rendering does not need it (the JPEG stream is the default transport).

Important

The launcher’s default image (apptainer/backend.sif) cannot render server-side, and neither can backend-conda.sif on POWER9. For the 3-D view to be rendered on the node, start the job with --sif backend-egl.sif. Without it the backend reports server-side rendering as unavailable and the desktop renders a decimated proxy of the cube locally.

Building the EGL image¶

conda-forge publishes VTK for linux-ppc64le only as the Qt/X11 build (9.2.6, 9.3.0, 9.3.1); the EGL and OSMesa variants exist for linux-64 only. The EGL definition is therefore a layer on the conda image that removes conda-forge’s VTK and its OpenGL libraries and builds VTK (tag v9.3.1 by default) headless with EGL, keeping everything else of the base. The build fails if vtkEGLRenderWindow is not built or not linked to libEGL.

In the directory that holds the conda image under the name backend-conda.sif (a symlink is enough):

ln -sf backend-conda-gpu.sif backend-conda.sif
apptainer build --force --fakeroot backend-egl.sif VisIVOVisualAnalytics/apptainer/backend-conda-egl.def

--force is needed, or Apptainer keeps the base image’s help and labels. APPTAINERENV_VTK_TAG selects another VTK tag. The definition estimates 70 to 90 minutes on 16 POWER9 cores; on PLEIADI-GPU, with 32 cores, it took about 20 minutes. Build where Apptainer’s temporary directory (APPTAINER_TMPDIR) is node-local, for example in a SLURM job on a compute node.

What the launcher adds for EGL¶

Every job (the bindings are harmless where the libraries do not exist) gets:

  • the host’s NVIDIA libraries (libEGL_nvidia, libcuda, libnvidia-*, from /usr/lib64 or /usr/lib/powerpc64le-linux-gnu) and the glvnd vendor file 10_nvidia.json, bound at their host paths, because Apptainer’s --nv misses several of them on some ppc64le installs; LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib64 and __EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES pointing at the NVIDIA vendor file;

  • XDG_CACHE_HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME and MPLCONFIGDIR under /tmp, because fontconfig takes a file lock in ~/.cache, and on an NFS-mounted home that lock can hang the first render for ever.

Node capacity under SLURM¶

The backend reads the memory it may use where it is true for its process (backend/app/node_status.py):

  1. the cgroup v2 hierarchy: memory.max and usage at its own cgroup and every ancestor it can see, the tightest limit winning;

  2. if no v2 memory files are readable, the cgroup v1 memory controller (memory.limit_in_bytes, memory.usage_in_bytes), as on older SLURM clusters;

  3. inside a SLURM job (SLURM_JOB_ID set), the memory SLURM granted as one more limit: SLURM_MEM_PER_NODE, or SLURM_MEM_PER_CPU times SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE. A grant counts even where the cluster does not enforce it with a cgroup; --mem=0 (the whole node) sets no cap;

  4. otherwise the host’s memory (/proc/meminfo).

Available memory is the limit minus the working set (usage without the reclaimable file cache), never more than the host has left. VISIVO_CGROUP_ROOT names the cgroup directory explicitly (and then cgroup v1 is not consulted).

This matters because the backend sizes its work by it rather than by the host’s RAM: the full-resolution threshold (see Large cube loading) is at most a quarter of that limit, the compute paths choose between holding a range in memory and streaming it from the available figure, and the node status that a catalogue ranks nodes on reports the same numbers (see The backend as an SRC node). A job given --mem 64G on a node with 512 GB is a 64 GB backend.

Server-side rendering on the node¶

With the EGL image, each remote 3-D view is a render session that runs in a child process of its own (backend/app/render_session/_process.py): VTK and the JPEG encoder then hold only that process’s GIL, so the backend keeps receiving commands and sending frames while the next frame is rendered, and a crash in VTK or the driver ends that session, not the backend.

Sessions are spread over the job’s GPUs in turn. EGL lists every GPU of the node whatever CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES says, so each session asks the driver for the CUDA device behind each EGL device (EGL_NV_device_cuda): only the job’s GPUs answer, and the session binds VTK to one of them through VTK_EGL_DEVICE_INDEX. If no EGL device has that extension, the backend logs a warning and VTK picks the device; if the mapping shows none of the node’s GPUs in the job, the session does not start.

Variable

Default

Meaning

VISIVO_RENDER_MAX_SESSIONS

8

Remote views the backend accepts at once; beyond it a new one is refused with HTTP 503.

VISIVO_RENDER_IDLE_TTL_SECONDS

300

A view with no command for this long is closed.

VISIVO_RENDER_IN_PROCESS

unset

1 renders in the backend’s own process instead (slower: rendering then holds the process that serves the WebSocket).

VTK_EGL_DEVICE_INDEX

unset

Binds every view to that EGL device instead of spreading them over the job’s GPUs.

How the view streams frames and lowers its quality while you rotate is described for users in the Cube viewer page. On PLEIADI-GPU (POWER9, V100), through an SSH tunnel, a 2540 x 1560 view of a 2 GB cube ran at about 26 frames per second once the drag level had settled; four views at once ran at 20.0 frames per second each when spread over four V100s, against 6.8 on one. The scripts that measure this and the recorded runs are in benchmark/remote_render.

A complete, recorded run on PLEIADI-GPU together with a SKAVA catalogue is described in the SKAVA documentation.

Troubleshooting¶

The job stays pending. The launcher waits VISIVO_ASSIGN_TIMEOUT seconds (300 by default) for SLURM to assign a node, then stops with no compute node assigned; the job stays queued and starts when the resources free up. The helper has recorded the job as soon as it was submitted, so --stop cancels it. To wait longer, set VISIVO_ASSIGN_TIMEOUT on the frontend; otherwise ask for fewer resources (a shorter --time, fewer GPUs, another --partition). A new run refuses to start while a job from an earlier run is still recorded: stop it first.

The backend does not become ready. The launcher polls for five minutes (ten for the Dask variant), then names the job log. Look there first: a missing image, a data root that does not exist, or a Python error at start.

The local port is in use. The helper refuses to start (localhost:<port> is already in use). Stop what holds it (often the desktop’s local backend on 8000) or choose another --port.

A tunnel from an earlier run is still active. The helper refuses to start until it is stopped: bash scripts/visivo_slurm_tunnel.sh --stop.

The tunnel dropped. The helper reopens it by itself within a few seconds of the connection ending, and keep-alives notice a dead connection within about a minute. If it does not come back, check that ssh <user>@<frontend> still works without a password, and that the job is still running: when the job ends (its --time is over) there is nothing left to tunnel to.

The desktop gets 401 from the cluster backend. The token in the desktop’s entry is not the job’s. Each job has its own token unless --token is given: copy it again from ~/.visivo_slurm_token (single node) or ~/.visivo_slurm_dask_token (Dask), never from ~/.visivo_token, which is the local backend’s. If the entry’s URL is a loopback address on the local backend’s port, the desktop sends it the local token, when there is one, whatever the entry says: use another --port.

The 3-D view is never rendered on the node. The backend has no EGL. The dataset-open response reports server_side_rendering_available: false, the Remote mode is disabled, and the desktop renders a decimated proxy of the cube locally. Start the job with --sif backend-egl.sif and a GPU (--gres). apptainer test backend-egl.sif runs the image’s own check, which fails when the backend would not offer server-side rendering.
